title: Abba, Father of Rabbi Simlai
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: In Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 5:3: when his son Rabbi Simlai came to Rabbi Yochanan asking him to teach him aggadah, he answered that he did not want to, because he was from Nehardea and lived in the South. In Pesachim 62b it is the reverse: that he was from Lod and his place of residence was Nehardea. Hyman prefers the Jerusalem Talmud’s reading, which he considers proven by Rosh Hashanah 20b, where Abba, the father of Rabbi Simlai, said to Shmuel: “Does the Master know this matter that was taught in the secret of intercalation?” — and it is known that Shmuel was in Nehardea. In Pesachim there, where he came before Rabbi Yochanan, Hyman proposes “before Rabbi Yonatan,” as in the Jerusalem Talmud. His son Rabbi Simlai was a student of Rabbi Yehudah Nesia; Hyman therefore places his father at the end of the days of the Tannaim, after Rabbi.

notes.text: The opposing birth/residence accounts remain separate. The Yonatan emendation and chronology are Hyman’s argument; his proof language is not a new independent establishment of identity.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 5:3 names Yonatan and describes Simlai as from Nehardea and living in the South. The consulted Bavli Pesachim 62b names Yochanan and has Lod as origin and Nehardea as residence. Rosh Hashanah 20b independently names Abba, Simlai’s father, speaking with Shmuel. Hyman’s preference, proposed emendation, proof language and chronology remain his argument rather than a silent harmonization.
